nodes.label: Rule Map (topic x class routing index)
FAI Cross-Class Invariants
nodes.rationale: True for every FAI class (best raw scores 1000; round score = normalised group score except F3B per-task partials; aggregate = sum minus drop-worst; penalties survive a dropped round) and false for at least one NZ class - carrying them into an NZ question is the likeliest wrong answer.

nodes.label: NZMAA Section 5 Soaring (separate NZ rulebook)
nodes.rationale: A separate rulebook by a separate body, not FAI variations; clause numbering collides with FAI so refs are written NZ.x.y.z. The FAI invariants do not hold for its classes.

nodes.label: Core Architectural Law: Competition Class model vs core system
nodes.rationale: The core system must not know about any specific competition class; all class variance is data in the class definition. If adding or changing a class requires editing code outside that class's own model, the core leaked a class-specific assumption and the design is wrong.

nodes.label: Immutable Event Log as Audit Trail
nodes.rationale: Club-level trusted tool: no auth, no score sign-off; an immutable event log of all mutations provides auditability instead.

nodes.label: BDD/Gherkin Acceptance Testing Approach
nodes.rationale: Once a feature reaches a real end-to-end user-facing workflow it is covered by Given/When/Then acceptance tests running against one store per run selected by SOARSCORE_TEST_STORE.

nodes.label: Property-Based Testing Discipline
nodes.rationale: Where a genuine invariant exists (draw fairness, score calculation, drop-worst, normalisation) name the invariant explicitly during planning so the property test stays meaningful.

nodes.label: tools/Soarscore.SeedData seed corpus
nodes.rationale: Seven FAI classes and three NZ ALES classes authored in C# are the model's test: anything they cannot express is a gap in the model; the NZ classes found four gaps the FAI corpus could not.

nodes.label: PublishedClassDefinition aggregate root
nodes.rationale: Code-level split of one domain concept added when the event-sourcing model was built: ClassDefinition is the pure value object rulebook; PublishedClassDefinition wraps it with content-hash identity and the events/fold logic Marten streams against.

nodes.label: Four Roots Not Three (Entry split rationale)
nodes.rationale: Keeping Entry inside Competition would make every score update load and lock the whole event; Entry split out as the unit of live capture keeps concurrent scorer writes independent - small aggregates referenced across boundaries by id.

nodes.label: Competition Class Notation Spec
nodes.rationale: Hand-writing notation isomorphic to the class diagram: one keyword per model element, no keyword that is not one, every rule-derived constant carries its source ref.

nodes.label: Notation Extensibility Findings F1-F28
nodes.rationale: Each finding is a place the model was short of something a rule requires; all resolved additively. Writing the seventh class (F3F) and the three NZ classes tested NFR-2 rather than asserting it.

nodes.label: flight.sequence intrinsic
nodes.rationale: The one intrinsic flight fact: which launch this flight was, 1-based. Grows only when a rule requires it with a citation; required by F5K launch penalties.

nodes.label: Hexagonal Architecture Principle
nodes.rationale: Onion layering with dependencies pointing inwards only: API adapter, Application ports/handlers, Domain aggregates.

nodes.label: Event Sourcing Principle
nodes.rationale: Events are the state and are immutable; read-model projections only for cross-stream queries; query-by-ID must fold the stream.

nodes.label: Intent-Based API Principle
nodes.rationale: Only POST commands and GET queries, paths to verbs not nouns, to decouple consumers from domain structures; never PUT/PATCH/DELETE/OPTIONS.

nodes.label: Headless Core Principle
nodes.rationale: No UI or alternative interaction; the system assumes no specific external UX requirements and is the kernel of a wider integrated competition system.

nodes.label: Core-Owned Invariants
nodes.rationale: Deliberately short list of rules true of every competition class (small field flies as one group; pipeline flight-local up to flight selection; annulled Entry has no result), each reached by trying to express an FAI rule as class data and concluding it did not belong there.

nodes.label: Adoption Check Inventory (16 checks)
nodes.rationale: Complete inventory of checks run once on adoption before a Competition may hold a rulebook; reasoning stays next to each construct in the notation and diagram docs.

nodes.label: Marten on PostgreSQL Decision
nodes.rationale: MIT licence satisfies open-source constraint; avoids ~1,400 LOC hand-rolled store plus SQLite footguns; Live aggregation expresses the query-by-ID-folds-stream rule exactly; bigserial/HWM gives ordering correctness for free. Counter-case recorded: we use roughly 15% of Marten at this scale.

nodes.label: Inline Projections Only (never async daemon)
nodes.rationale: Required rather than convenient: Person email uniqueness is enforced at the unique-index level and an async projection cannot reject concurrent duplicates; inline also gives read-your-own-writes which the POST-command-then-GET-query shape needs.

nodes.label: Read Model Inventory (people, competitions, class_library, entry_index)
nodes.rationale: Projections index which streams exist where and are never a source of truth; scores are never projected because materialising a leaderboard would re-implement the Competition Class model outside its one place.

nodes.label: Fisher SQLite Backend
nodes.rationale: Second backend cost one composition root plus a thin subclass - measured, not estimated; proving a backend means running the same suites unchanged against both stores.

nodes.label: AppendExpectedVersion Seam (sixth seam)
nodes.rationale: Marten reads expectedVersion as the version AFTER the append, Fisher as BEFORE; answering wrongly does not throw but silently disables the concurrency guard, so the member is protected abstract with no default - a third backend must state its answer.

nodes.label: Canonical JSON Definition Format
nodes.rationale: Seed classes enter through the same door as user POSTs: emitting JSON at build and ingesting at runtime closes the bypass gap and makes checked-in seed JSON reviewable as exactly what a user would POST.

nodes.label: Content Hash Identity (no version pinning)
nodes.rationale: Makes replay provable (a 2028 re-score can demonstrate it read the same bytes) and drift detectable; replaces version pinning which only worked if nobody edited seed data in place.

nodes.label: Single Ingestion Path
nodes.rationale: Input is untrusted: Validate is total and non-throwing returning every defect, Defect renders as an API error body, input limits guard DoS, and no code execution ever - the definition is data.

nodes.label: Citations Not In The Model (decided, rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rule references are an authoring-side property; any format the core recognised would be a class-specific assumption, since F3K.7, NZ.3.12.3 and a club bylaw are all legitimate citations the core could never interpret.

nodes.label: Hand-Rolled IDispatcher (~60 LOC)
nodes.rationale: Zero licence risk and more inspectable than a behaviour pipeline; MediatR rejected on commercial licence v12+.

nodes.label: Minimal API MapCommand/MapQuery Routes
nodes.rationale: Controllers pull toward noun-resources; helpers turn the intent-based rule into a failing build via a reflection test asserting every route is GET or POST.

nodes.label: $kind Polymorphic Discriminator (System.Text.Json)
nodes.rationale: A discriminator named kind shadows a real property, emits both keys with no error and fails only on read-back; AllowOutOfOrderMetadataProperties on ingestion and byte-comparing round-trip tests were forced by silent spike failures.

nodes.label: NFR-1 One Centralised Flexible Competition Class Model
NFR-2 Additive-Only Extensibility
nodes.rationale: Closed vocabulary keeps static validation at adoption and deterministic re-scoring; an open expression language would satisfy the letter while destroying both. Term types admitted only when a class's rules require them, cited.

nodes.label: NFR-4 No Imposed Ordering On Score Capture
nodes.rationale: Nothing waits for round N's scores before round N+1 proceeds; validity is structural not temporal and results derive from what is present. The CD marking a task-round complete closes capture explicitly and reversibly.

nodes.label: AdoptedRules value object
nodes.rationale: The whole rulebook copied into Competition at creation; scoring reads this never the library class, so editing or deleting a library class cannot perturb a running or finished event.

nodes.label: RulesAmendment
nodes.rationale: Applies retroactively to the whole competition; costs nothing because results are derived - the next query returns corrected numbers.

nodes.label: ParameterBinding
nodes.rationale: Recorded as events precisely because re-scoring must reproduce the decisions as they were actually taken.

nodes.label: ReflightRuling
nodes.rationale: Where the rulebook is silent the silence is filled by a recorded ruling, never an assumption; valid before any entry is captured and superseded rather than replaced.

nodes.label: Annulment
nodes.rationale: Exists because of F3F.1.5's provisional re-flight: the competitor re-flies under protest and the jury later decides which attempt stands - ReflightSelection cannot express a per-instance jury decision.

nodes.label: MeasuredValue (number or flag)
nodes.rationale: Measurements are not all numbers: rules require plain observations such as landed-in-area alongside quantities.

nodes.label: ScoringService domain service
nodes.rationale: Reads the rulebook from the Competition's own copy and raw data from Entries; has no consistency boundary of its own and spans two roots, not three, because the library class is absent from the scoring path.

nodes.label: ResultState (Valid / NoResult)
nodes.rationale: NoResult is not a score of zero: in a task where the fastest time wins, a raw zero would otherwise win the group outright.

nodes.label: PhaseDefinition
nodes.rationale: No mandatory flag: mandatoriness there is conditional on event level, which nothing in the model represents; readmitting needs that concept first.

nodes.label: DropPolicy
nodes.rationale: Ordered list, first match wins; may be empty because discarding nothing has an identity value and nine of sixteen phases have no discard to state.

nodes.label: ReflightRule
nodes.rationale: Two roles one event: entitled competitor takes the reflight even if worse, everyone else takes better of two; default at class, override at task where rules differ.

nodes.label: PenaltyDefinition
nodes.rationale: Carries effects not merely a cost because zeroing a flight/round/task are real outcomes; exclusionGroups is a list because exclusion is pairwise not an equivalence class (F28); suppression computed in one pass from accrued contributions.

nodes.label: RateTerm
nodes.rationale: cap clamps the metric consumed, not the points produced - they coincide only at 1 pt/s, which is why the rules write them as if the same thing.

nodes.label: PiecewiseTerm
nodes.rationale: Bands evaluated over (metric - origin); F5K launch points are per metre relative to an announced height, which is the whole of finding F5.

nodes.label: Band (cumulative piecewise band)
nodes.rationale: Bands are cumulative: 1 pt/s to 600 s then -1 pt/s scores 599 at 601 s - lets one term type express both F3B overtime deduction and F5J two-slope height penalty.

nodes.label: Predicate (Comparison / AllOf)
nodes.rationale: Conjunction only, no anyOf: every multi-condition site is a conjunction and disjunction is readmitted with the first rule that cites it. Not an expression language so definitions stay statically validatable at adoption.

nodes.label: TaskTiming
nodes.rationale: workingTime populated iff kind is Fixed; under UntilAllFlightsComplete the round ends when the last flight does - recording a guessed end time would be a fabricated fact.

nodes.label: GroupConstraint
nodes.rationale: Absent means the class does not group-score at all; minPerGroup as ParameterRef means it does and the size is open. minPerGroup 1 was a fabricated rule that also told the draw a group of one is acceptable.

nodes.label: Normalisation
nodes.rationale: Optional (F25): absent means the task does not normalise, the raw score is the result. There is no identity normalisation, so writing one to satisfy a multiplicity would have been a fabricated rule.

nodes.label: Fixed Scoring Pipeline Stages
nodes.rationale: Pipeline is fixed and core-owned; every stage takes class data. Classes disagree about where things happen, which is why the order is explicit; zero-effects land at the raw-score end and deduct/disqualify at apply penalties.

nodes.label: Competition Class (glossary)
nodes.rationale: Everything that differs between one type of contest and another lives here and nowhere else; the rest of the system reads a class without ever knowing which one it is.

nodes.label: Parameter (glossary)
nodes.rationale: Values the class declares but deliberately does not fix, so a legitimate local choice does not require a separate rulebook per combination.

nodes.label: Score Term (glossary)
nodes.rationale: Terms exist so the system can carry out a class's arithmetic without knowing what the numbers mean - a landing table and a launch-height penalty are the same kind of term reading different measurements.

nodes.label: Entry (glossary)
nodes.rationale: One competitor's turn within a group; isolated as its own aggregate because it is what scorers directly update at high concurrency - a reflight is simply a second Entry pointing at whichever group flew it.

nodes.label: Measurement (glossary)
nodes.rationale: Recorded exactly as captured and never altered; corrections are recorded alongside so results can always be verified and scores recalculated at any time.

nodes.label: Score (glossary)
nodes.rationale: Scores are computed not captured; derivable from raw record plus rules so they can be re-run after protest, correction or query and produce identical placings.

nodes.label: Finalisation (glossary)
nodes.rationale: Captures what was declared, never what is the score; captured results can always be re-derived and compared against what was published, making evaluator changes visible instead of silent.

nodes.label: Scorer (user role)
nodes.rationale: Records raw metrics only, no interpretation at capture; one Scorer per competitor; free to record when they can - nothing about the contest's running may depend on their being up to date.

nodes.label: Gliderscore Concept Gaps (team scoring, series, merged comps)
nodes.rationale: None of these enter the glossary without explicit approval per house rules; if wanted they belong as backlog story stubs first.

hyperedges.label: Scoring derives results from adopted rules plus raw entries
Closed score-term vocabulary implementing NFR-2 arithmetic
Dual-backend event store strategy via JasperFx shared contracts
